kicker: It job-hunts overnight. Kisuke serves the shortlist with breakfast.
description: A job-discovery service that pulls listings overnight from ATS boards, Polish job sites, and HN Who's Hiring, normalizes wildly different payloads into one schema (raw kept verbatim, normalized rebuilt on demand), scores them with explainable config-driven rules, and hands the shortlist to Kisuke's morning brief through a shared Postgres. Feedback loops back — dismissed jobs stay gone. After the job hunt: same pipeline, pointed at GitHub, surfacing OSS issues worth contributing to via polling and signed webhooks.
detail_description: Job hunting is a discovery problem, not a bookkeeping one — the work is finding the good openings, not typing them into a tracker. JobBoards does the finding: a nightly BullMQ pipeline fetches from Greenhouse/Lever/Ashby boards for a company watchlist, justjoin.it and NoFluffJobs for the Polish market, and HN's monthly Who's Hiring thread for free-text extraction with honest confidence scores.

The architecture centers on a raw/normalized split: every payload is captured verbatim, and the normalized table is a disposable derivation that can be rebuilt from raw at any time — so normalization bugs are fixable retroactively. Dedupe rides on provider identity, delistings are detected by absence sweeps (never deleted), and every score carries a per-rule breakdown so 'why did this surface?' always has an answer.

Integration is deliberately boring: the service is sole writer of its own tables in the shared Kisuke Postgres, and Kisuke reads them when composing its 05:05 morning brief. The interesting parts are in the plumbing — idempotent ingestion, storage-level atomic claims for webhook processing, HMAC-verified GitHub deliveries, timing-safe API auth.

It's also a workflow experiment: the whole build runs as a GitHub ticket board — one issue per ticket, one branch per issue, squash-merged only after a review covering correctness, failure modes, and TypeScript idiom. And it outlives the job hunt: the OSS phase points the same pipeline at GitHub so the mornings switch from 'jobs worth applying to' to 'issues worth contributing to'.
